created_by: ChatGPT: AI-assisted source inspection and transcription
purpose: Six document-content attributions, not a definition of democracy, a regime classification, or a sample representative of world political traditions.
limits: Passages were inspected against official-source transcriptions and a UN General Assembly text hosted by Refworld. No independent human review, legal-effect analysis, historical implementation claim or fact-promotion is implied. Proposition text is a bounded paraphrase, not a quotation. These new IDs do not silently replace the 100 unsourced conversation drafts.

nodes.name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948 text)
Joint resolution proposing the Nineteenth Amendment (1919 text)
Participation directly or through chosen representatives
nodes.text: Each person has a right to participate in their country's government, either directly or through freely selected representatives.
nodes.population: Everyone, in relation to their own country, as addressed by Article 21(1).

nodes.name: Popular authority and electoral conditions
nodes.text: Governmental authority should rest on the people's will, expressed in genuine, periodic elections with universal and equal voting rights and either a secret ballot or an equivalent free voting procedure.
nodes.population: The people and governmental authority addressed by Article 21(3).

nodes.name: Peaceful assembly and association
nodes.text: Each person has a right to assemble peacefully and to associate with others.

nodes.name: Consent as the source of just governmental powers
nodes.text: Governments obtain their just powers from the consent of those they govern.
nodes.population: The governed, as described in the 1776 Declaration; no historical electorate is inferred.

nodes.name: House selection interval and elector qualifications
nodes.text: House members are to be chosen every two years by the people of the states; each state's electors must meet the qualifications for electors of its most numerous legislative branch.
nodes.population: House members and state electors addressed by Article I, Section 2, first paragraph; not all residents.

nodes.name: Proposed prohibition of sex-based voting-rights denial
nodes.text: Neither the United States nor a state may deny or restrict US citizens' voting rights because of sex.
nodes.population: US citizens and the federal/state authorities addressed by the proposed amendment text.
